newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Hansa, Saku awaken Estonian bourse from slumber.
newsitem.headline: Hansa, Saku awaken Estonian bourse from slumber.

text.p: Estonian bourse activity picked up briefly on Wednesday with Hansapank's May results and Saku's decision to release its first quarter figures prodding the market out of its listless state.
Total trade on the main list was 16.1 million kroons with the Talse 0.54 percent up at 250.38.
"The market is still suffering from low liquidity, so even small trades seem to make prices move further than we would normally expect, but the higlights were Hansapank and Saku," one dealer said.
"It was active in the morning, but most of Hansa's gains fell away, as did Tallinna Farma's a week ago," he added.
"Not even really good news can move and hold the market," a trader said.
Hansapank rose 1.25 kroons to 128.75 kroons on trade worth 6.5 million kroons after reaching a high of 130 kroons after it released its May results.
Saku Brewery's decision to release its first quarter results also inspired a brief flurry of activity as the stock's price rose by 1.25 kroons to 35.25 kroons on 2.4 million kroons.
Saku had earlier said that it would not release its first quater results as demanded by the bourse, causing the stock's price to drop by 17 percent in one day's trading.
The free market turned over 4.7 million kroons and Saku was the most active.
